News.title: Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Red Roses’ 39-match winning streak brought to end in Canada draw
News.content:
The record books will show that this meeting, a proper Test full of ebbs and flows, was neither. And, no matter the pre-match belief of England head coach John Mitchell, Canada are not on the same level of professionalism and funding as his side. Mitchell had brought back nine players, many of whom featured in last year’s World Cup final victory, after the thrashing of Australia last week with the expectation that the history of 2025 would repeat itself. Canada had other ideas.

“The plan on the field at the last scrum was to go for the win,” Canada captain Sophie de Goede said. “And then the message came on from the sideline to kick it out. In that moment you have to trust your coach and your coaching staff, and we’ll have a discussion about it later. If we had given away a penalty off the next breakdown, we’d be sitting here going, ‘Why didn’t you kick it out?’”

England’s downfall came at the set-piece, where their line-out malfunctioned and their scrum never gained dominance, in a tale which was not too dissimilar to last week. The hosts came second in the physical battle, too, which was uncharacteristic of them; losing Hannah Botterman to a shoulder injury did not help, either. All told, Canada just looked as though they wanted it a little bit more and maybe this was the wake-up call the Red Roses needed: when you are at the top, and at the top by a margin, every team want to be the one to dethrone you.

News.title: All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper
News.content:
It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”

News.title: GPs summoned in Frankfurt as third malaria death reported
News.content:
While malaria is treatable if caught early, the patients were likely not considered to have the disease because they lacked travel history to countries where malaria typically circulates, meaning treatment was delayed.

“This is why we alerted the medical people in Frankfurt, if you have odd cases presenting at your clinic, please also consider that there might be malaria around,” Dr Tinnemann said.

“There is this assumption that people who get sick with a nasty fever in places like Frankfurt and elsewhere that have not travelled cannot have malaria, and we don’t bother to investigate. That’s got to stop. That’s why these people die,” Joe Lines, Professor of Malaria Control and Vector Biology at the London School of Tropical Hygiene and Medicine, told The Telegraph.

Before the two cases in Schwanheim – both of which occurred at least 3 miles from the airport where the first malaria cases were reported – investigators were working on the hypothesis that just a single mosquito was responsible for the outbreak, but the new cases have cast doubt on that theory.

“We expect mosquitoes to live between one and three weeks on average,” said Dr Tinnemann.

“We had five cases in the beginning of July, then another in August - at that point, there was a good chance that potentially it could just be one bug. But now it seems at least there must be one other,” he said.

Frankfurt’s public health board have now shipped blood samples from all eight patients to a specialised lab in Antwerp, Belgium, where scientists can carry out DNA analysis to indicate if the infections came from one or multiple mosquitoes, and are awaiting results.

As temperatures warm, experts fear that several tropical mosquito-borne diseases – including malaria, dengue fever, Zika virus, and chikungunya could become established across Europe.

Earlier this month, a colony of Aedes aeypti mosquitoes – the bugs responsible for transmitting dengue and Zika virus – were found breeding in a residential area in East London for the first time.

Airfinity, the disease-monitoring company, said of the malaria outbreak in Frankfurt: “the risk to the wider public remains low but non-zero.”

“Continued vector surveillance, rapid diagnosis, and ready access to antimalarials are critical to prevent further severe outcomes.”

News.title: Global fund utilises AI to tackle malaria, TB, and HIV amid aid cuts
News.content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is helping to soften the blow from aid cuts, according to one of the world’s biggest development funds.

The Global Fund, which raises and invests billions of pounds to reduce the burden of HIV, tuberculosis (TB) and malaria globally says new AI-driven products like portable pregnancy scanners are helping to mitigate the funding gap.

“[We] have adapted pretty quickly to the changes in the funding environment; it has undoubtedly had negative impacts on health outcomes [...], but in some ways, the resilience of life-saving services has been remarkable,” Peter Sands, the executive director of the Global Fund, told The Telegraph.

The Global Fund is managing a $6 billion (£4.4bn) shortfall for the period 2026 to 2028 and has been forced to make difficult decisions to continue their work, it confirmed this week.

The gap comes as Western governments shift money from foreign aid to defence. The UK reduced its contribution to the fund by 15 per cent last year to £850 million, down from £1 billion.

But Mr Sands said investments in tools to tackle infectious diseases – including those driven by AI – are starting to pay off.

“Innovation is absolutely part of the answer when money is short. One of the few ways you can get to make the money go further is to have a better tool, a better way of doing things,” Mr Sands said.

News.title: Thomas Tuchel faces fight to win trust of England players
News.content:
Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

Bournemouth vs Liverpool preview

Andoni Iraola will hope to preserve his unbeaten run as Liverpool manager when he visits the Vitality Stadium today.

The Spanish coach has enjoyed a reasonable start to life on Merseyside, going all six competitive matches without defeat.

But he’s not set the world alight. A return of six points from his first four Premier League matches is something of a disappointment, as is failing to win either of their two opening league matches for the third time in 63 years.

Successive draws against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest were followed by two solid wins, especially the latter in the Champions League against Atletico Madrid.



But Liverpool were unable to build on that momentum when failing to score against Fulham, a side who have already shipped seven times this season.

A much-changed starting XI dispatched Tottenham in midweek, and Iraola will hope his rested side can travel south and take the spoils in a fixture they’ve enjoyed over the years.

Last season’s 3-2 defeat aside, Liverpool have won the last six meetings with Bournemouth by an aggregate scoreline of 18-4. In fact, of their last 15 meetings, the Reds have won 13 times.

Life for Iraola’s replacement, Marco Rose, hasn’t exactly got off to a flying start either.



Rose is yet to taste victory in the Premier League after four matches, drawing the last three against Everton, Newcastle and Brentford.

The biggest disappointment for Rose will have been the fact his side were in winning positions in all of those fixtures, three of which they held until the 84th minute, only to be undone late on.

Nevertheless, the Vitality has been something of a fortress in recent times, with Bournemouth unbeaten in their last 12 on home turf, a run stretching back to January 3 when they were beaten narrowly by Arsenal.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta claims Arsenal ‘didn’t respect any principle of play’ in horror defeat at Brighton
Sports.content:

MIKEL ARTETA admitted Arsenal were given a “lesson” by Brighton as their winning start went up in smoke.

And the stunned Gunners boss knew they faced a tough day at the Amex after ONE minute.



It was Arsenal’s biggest Prem loss for more than three years — which also came against the Seagulls — following goals from Pascal Gross, Charalampos Kostoulas and Chema Andres.

Arteta said: “I am extremely disappointed. It’s a big lesson for us and they deserved to win.



“We have to congratulate them for the victory.

“There were certain basics you need in football — especially in the Premier League — that we were very far from.



“It was the amount of technical errors we made, while we didn’t respect any principle of play that we have to do.

“But that’s not going to take away what the boys have done in the last six or seven weeks since the World Cup.”

Arsenal had won all six games this season and conceded just one before Saturday’s shocker.

Andres’ header, his first goal in English football, sealed Arsenal’s heaviest defeat since a 3-0 home loss to Roberto De Zerbi’s Brighton in May 2023.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The champions are now second in the Prem table on goal difference behind Manchester City — whose game in hand is against Sunderland on Sunday.

Asked when he knew Arsenal had a problem, Arteta said: “From the first throw-in, you could sense it, it was so clear.

“We put ourselves in trouble one time, two times, three times.

“That’s one of the biggest lessons we have to take from this game.

“We know what it takes to win every match — and we know what it’s going to take to win against Leeds when we come back.



“That doesn’t take away the disappointment that we feel right now.”

The victory capped an epic week for Brighton on the day they celebrated their 125th anniversary.

Arsenal ratings v Brighton ARSENAL players were outplayed on the South Coast as they fell to their first defeat of the season with a 3-0 drubbing. Brighton looked by far the better team as they took a three-goal lead at the Amex Stadium. Here’s how SunSport’s Simon Collings rated the Gunners at The Amex Stadium…

The Seagulls have scored SIXTEEN goals — the most in the top flight — and boss Fabian Hurzeler toasted a “complete” team performance.

He declared: “It is a special result against the champions.



“Congratulations to a special club for the history and everyone involved in its past and now the present.”

Sports.title: ‘Big future’ – Michael Carrick backs two struggling Man Utd stars after horror show against Brighton
Sports.content:
Next

THE LAST time Manchester United lost at Fulham, Michael Carrick was playing at centre half.

That 3-0 reverse in December 2009 came amid a defensive injury crisis that resulted in the rarity of a Sir Alex Ferguson back three.



But the trio were Carrick, Darren Fletcher and Ritchie de Laet. Two midfielders and a full back. De Laet never played for United again.

United also shipped three goals in midweek against Brighton, albeit Carrick picked conventional back four.



It did not look that way in one of the most diabolical defensive performances Old Trafford has hosted in recent times.

Overall, United have conceded ten goals in six games, with their only clean sheet against Champions League minnows Sabah.

Leny Yoro is into his third year at United after they gazumped Real Madrid to sign him in a £58.91million coup. The centre back is still only 20 but eventually has to assume senior status in a backline that is set to be overhauled next.

Ayden Heaven was, and remains, a rawer recruit. But Heaven turns 20 next week and celebrates two years at United in the New Year.

Ruben Amorim once said Heaven is “sometimes too relaxed”. He sleepwalked through the Brighton debacle.

Carrick said of the pair: “I thought they started really well, actually, in the game.



Man Utd ratings vs Brighton: Lacey a shining light on dark evening as Heaven and Yoro ripped apart MANCHESTER UNITED suffered a humiliating Carabao Cup exit at Old Trafford as Brighton came from two goals down to reach the last 16. It is the first time in 50 years that United have held a 2-0 lead at Old Trafford and lost the game. The Red Devils were in dreamland after early goals from Shea Lacey and Mason Mount, before the Seagulls took control and mounted a stunning comeback. United have not won a domestic cup match since beating Leicester in the FA Cup in February 2025 and again crashed out at first attempt of the Carabao Cup following last season’s horror show at Grimsby. Michael Carrick is feeling the heat after goals Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper ended one of two potential trophy hopes this season. Here’s how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated the United players from Old Trafford, as Brighton picked up a fifth straight victory in M16...

“I thought we started really well, so it’s not about them.

“I think they’ll learn from different experiences and they’ve done particularly well and they’re in a really good spot, two young players that have got really good futures.

“So unfortunately you go through times in football and you have some good spells and sometimes you learn a lot from the things that didn’t go so well.

“But I wouldn’t isolate them at all from the other night.”

Yoro was sidelined for the first four months of his United career with a metatarsal fracture sustained in his second appearance, but he was largely injury-free last season.



Harry Maguire turns 34 in March, Matthijs de Ligt has been out since November and Lisandro Martinez has entered the final year of his contract. Time is of the essence for Yoro to mature.

Carrick disagrees. “No, not necessarily, no.

“He’s 20, Leny, and again in context, he’s got a fantastic future ahead of him and a lot of potential.

“He’s learning, he’s developing. To be at this club and play as a centre back at such a young age is a challenging position. It’s one that he can do for sure, it’s one that Ayden can do for sure.



“But there’s no cut off point. Some players progress and find when they’re 18 they’re at that level where they can really perform.

“Some players like Leny showed that he can perform, I’ve got no worries for Leny, I think he does a lot of really good things and he’s part of learning.

“Sometimes it might be 20, sometimes you see players 22, 23, 24 where they start developing, so there’s definitely no cut-off point.

“He’s just got to keep progressing and moving in the right direction, wanting to learn, keep improving, getting more opportunities.



“He’s doing a lot of good things, and I think we’ve got to be careful again, and I certainly won’t do it, is make knee-jerk decisions on certain players just because of one game or one half or one moment in a game.

“And we’ve got a lot of belief in Leny, for sure.”

Yoro and Heaven have the benefit of working with backroom staff members Jonny Evans and Jonathan Woodgate, who were bedded into the United and Leeds defences at young ages.

Evans, 38, entered a dressing room that had Rio Ferdinand, Nemanja Vidic, Gary Neville, Wes Brown, John O’Shea and Patrice Evra in it, senior professionals and serial winners to guide him.



“Leny’s fortunate he has got some really good coaches that have lived it and understand his position,” Carrick acknowledged. “And Leny’s got a big future ahead of him.

“Sometimes learning in the moment it’s tough. Other times he’s done particularly well, so we keep developing, we keep learning.

“He’s in a good place, he’s got a big future.”

Carrick will almost certainly recall Maguire and Martinez at Craven Cottage. Luke Shaw could return after a two-week absence.



If Shaw is a risk, it is one worth taking. Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui were dire deputies at left back against Manchester City and Brighton and United do not play again until October 10.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It’s certainly not the start we wanted, in that respect,” Carrick admitted of United’s defensive record.

“We need to improve, no doubt, as a team collectively. It’s not just a backline or certainly a goalkeeper, it’s a collective thing.”

Sports.title: Michael Carrick still has ‘faith’ in controversial VAR despite shock decision that cost Man United in derby defeat
Sports.content:
Next

MICHAEL CARRICK still has “faith” in VAR but is adamant Manchester City’s winner will not define Manchester United’s season.

Pro Ref acknowledged there was a “lack of judgement” hours after Erling Haaland’s derby winner last Sunday and chief Howard Webb admitted he was “really disappointed”.



In audio released of the review, VAR Matt Donohue did not once consider the offside status of Enzo Fernandez, who attempted to connect with Josko Gvardiol’s deflected cross that Haaland converted from.

Privately, Carrick was staggered that nobody alerted Donohue to the fact that Fernandez was interfering with play.



An assistant VAR and replay operator were dialled into the audio with Donohue.

Carrick stressed the apology United received was “meaningless” but respected Webb’s swiftness in acknowledging the error.

“One-off things can happen,” Carrick said. “At the time it was a pretty big one, we know that, I don’t think I need to go over that.

“I’ve got faith in it, of course. It’s the system that we work towards and that we use, so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.

“I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens, it does happen, but moving forward we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us.

“And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“But that was a pretty big one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”

The 1-0 loss to City was followed by United’s collapse from 2-0 up to lose 3-2 to Brighton in the League Cup third round on Wednesday, marking the first time Carrick has suffered successive defeats in charge of the club.

Fulham host United in the Premier League on Sunday and are yet to record a league win this term. United have also not lost at Craven Cottage since December 2009.

A third successive loss would fuel uncertainty around Carrick’s future ahead of a three-week international break, but he is determined to not let the Haaland goal kibosh United’s campaign.

Carrick stressed: “It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a big impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season.



“That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible.”

Sports.title: Ex-Chelsea manager Liam Rosenior has to be held back after furiously goading Strasbourg fans with new club
Sports.content:
Next

LIAM ROSENIOR had to be held back in a mass brawl after furiously goading Strasbourg fans.

The ex-Chelsea boss, 42, returned to Ligue 1 after his Stamford Bridge sacking.



He took over at Paris FC in July and faced former employers Strasbourg for the first time on Saturday.

Paris ran out 2-1 winners to maintain their unbeaten start to the season.



And it gave Rosenior extra satisfaction to get the three points against Chelsea’s BlueCo sister club.

While Rosenior was popular with some of the Strasbourg fans during his stint in Alsace, there were many who saw him as a by-product of the hated BlueCo regime.



And after the full-time whistle on Saturday – following stick from the away fans at Stade Jean-Bouin – he could not resist giving some back.

Rosenior passionately and elaborately celebrated, wildly waved his arms and defiantly beat his chest in front of the away end.

He then flung his hands to gesticulate as well.

And that sparked chaos.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Strasbourg’s fans booed angrily while many of their players rushed over to confront Rosenior as a giant shoving match erupted.

The manager was in the thick of the melee and appeared to push someone away before being manhandled by a member of security and ushered away.

He then continued his celebrations in front of his own Paris fans – who were loving his emboldened antics.

But Rosenior was quizzed on the incident in his media interviews and revealed he was responding to those who went “too far” and “disrespected” his family.



The ex-Fulham, Hull and Brighton full-back said in his press conference: “A small section of the Strasbourg supporters disrespected my family.



“I understand the context of what they were singing. My bench were visibly upset.

“It was a small section.

“Strasbourg is a fantastic football club with great people who work for the club and great people who support the club.

“For me to celebrate in that way was a message to a group of people who never wanted me to be successful at that club.”

He added to Ligue1+: “The people in the club who know me know that I’ve always been respectful, and I still do want the best for that football club.



“When I heard the chants, I know [them], I understand French. I understand the context, the language, and that was a step too far.

“There are a lot of things that have happened.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I celebrated in the way that I did for many reasons.”

Sports.title: Fleming wants England back top of Test rankings as 'work to be done' on discipline
Sports.content:
New England Test head coach Stephen Fleming has spoken of his desire to return the team to the top of the world rankings, adding that there is "work to be done" on the side's disciplinary issues that have dominated headlines this summer.

In June, Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson were suspended from the second Test of the 2-1 series loss to New Zealand due to a nightclub incident that occurred in the wake of their opening win at Lord's.

Last month, Brydon Carse was handcuffed outside a nightclub in Derby and missed the second and third Tests of England's series whitewash of Pakistan, prompting Test captain Joe Root to describe himself as "hacked off" by the growing list of alcohol-related incidents involving England players.

Carse did not face any charges after police closed their investigation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We take a look back at an extraordinary summer of Test series which saw Ben Stokes retire, a new England captain, the end of Bazball, and a series sweep of Pakistan

"It's disappointing," Fleming said. "The way that players represent England and the group is going to be really important to me."

He added: "I watched Joe in the press conference, and when he voices his displeasure at the behaviour, I think that said it all.

"If you want a great example of how to behave as an international cricketer, Joe Root is it.

"There's work to be done, and that comes back to making sure we're tying into something a bit bigger than oneself."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fleming discusses his method of discipline, with England having seen a number of off-field incidents for players over the last year

As well as having "a lot of contact" with Root since accepting the Test job on July 30 and throughout the Pakistan series - which Fleming was not yet in post for, due to family and commercial commitments - the new coach said he had also been in touch with Stokes, who retired from international cricket in June.

Amid suggestions of a possible return for the home Ashes series next summer, Fleming said of the 35-year-old: "He's really happy and seemed to be really at peace with his decision.

"My view is that when a player decides to retire, it's a big decision, and I have the utmost respect for that decision."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stokes reflects on his decision to retire from international cricket and explains why it was the right time

Fleming excited for Ashes and keen to take England to top

Fleming admitted he is already excited about coaching England in next summer's Ashes, calling it "an absolute highlight", while he also talked up the potential of the team he is about to take over.

"I would love to be in charge of the number one Test team in the world. That would be my aspiration," Fleming said.

"My honest appraisal is it's a great time to be the head coach. I think it's a real opportunity with the players that are coming through.

It's one of the most prestigious jobs in cricket, and I was very honoured to be asked... The opportunity to take up this role is one that you don't turn down.

"The fast bowlers as an example, I loved watching them operate in the [Pakistan] Test series recently.

"Also, the introduction of [Jordan] Cox and [Dan] Lawrence was nice, when you've got someone like [Jacob] Bethell [to come back].

"There's talent there competing for places, and that's always the barometer. If you're leaving very good players out, then you're going to be in a healthy situation."

Image: Jordan Cox (left) and Dan Lawrence (right) impressed during the Pakistan Test series

Fleming added on the World Test Championship, in which England sit sixth in the 2025-2027 cycle - having failed to reach the final of any of the previous three editions: "I think England could do much better in that.

"If that's one of the pinnacle trophies in world cricket, why would we not be trying to get it, along with every other marquee event that comes our way?

"That opportunity is real, but there's a huge amount of work to do."

Fleming rejects 'Flemball' in pursuit of 'cricket sense'

As for the playing style Fleming will look for his team to adopt, he was keen to praise the prior work of Stokes and former New Zealand team-mate - England's current white-ball coach - Brendon McCullum, but said he is looking to "combine a little bit of cricket sense around some key moments".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fleming says the end of Bazball was 'chaotic' and that he was disappointed for outgoing captain Stokes

There will be no 'Bazball' style moniker to accompany his team's style, however, as per his predecessor.

"That's a medical condition," Fleming joked when presented with the prospect of 'Flemball'.

"The way they [Stokes and McCullum] changed the nature of Test cricket was quite remarkable, and I have a huge amount of respect for the courage that that took.

"Obviously, the last 12 months it hasn't evolved as they would have liked and the fans would have liked, but I still acknowledge that period of two years [prior]."

He added: "I really loved the positive play and the freeing up of the England players, so if I could take that and combine a little bit of cricket sense around some key moments.

"There are key times in a match that you have to be really smart, and maybe we can just work a bit harder on that - but still combine positive nature of the players that are in there."

Root is 'greatness' and 'the best guy to captain Test team'

Talking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast, Fleming elaborated further on the respect he has for Root and how delighted he is to have him as captain of the Test team.

Root had previously captained England from 2017-2022 before being replaced by Stokes following a barren run of one win in his last 17 Tests.

Upon Stokes' resignation, white-ball skipper Harry Brook could have been an all-format option, but Fleming is thrilled that Root accepted the role again.

"I am a really big fan of Root," Fleming said. "I think he is a wonderful player and ambassador for the game, so to work with him was really appealing.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Root hailed England's adaptability with the bat and his high-quality bowling attack after the team stormed to a Test series win over Pakistan in his first series back as captain

"I just knew that he is the best guy to captain this side. He epitomises everything that is great about an international player. He is greatness, but a wonderful human being in the way that he conducts himself and can go about being great.

"He is such a great role model and such a perfect person for a young group of players. It was a no-brainer, for me, for him to be captain.

"Root is in charge. If he is going out and making key decisions, he is in charge. My role is very closely linked to provide him with what he needs. That can be criticism, constructively, so it's not just a yes position.

"I want him to be the best he can be and I think there is still room to grow in his captaincy with this group. I don't necessarily know what that looks like but I know there is growth and that's exciting."

Sports.title: McIlroy two off  Wentworth lead and ready to 'play aggressively'
Sports.content:
Manuel Elvira and Filippo Celli share the lead heading into the final round of the BMW PGA Championship after they both made birdies on the 18th to move one ahead at Wentworth.

Rather remarkably, 20 players will go into Sunday within four shots of the lead, including Rory McIlroy, who produced a box-office finish, sending the patrons into delirium on the 18th by making an eagle to move within two shots of the pace-setting duo at 11 under par.

McIlroy equalled four other players - Adam Scott, Joaquin Niemann, Davis Bryant and Kristoffer Reitan - to finish tied for sixth on the leaderboard through 54 holes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy made an incredible final-hole eagle on day three of the BMW PGA Championship

In windy conditions, Spain's Alejandro Del Rey and American duo Johannes Veerman and JJ Spaun had all been tied with Celli and Elvira at 12 under par late in the third round.

Del Rey and Veerman had enjoyed epic days on the course, each shooting low scores of eight-under 64 to shoot up the leaderboard.

Celli, however, rose to make four birdies on his back nine, to jump above the chasing pack, alongside Elvira, and benefitted from an incredible bit of luck on his last hole.

His approach shot ricocheted off a wooden bulkhead lining the stream and somehow missed the water, instead skirting into the greenside bunker. From there he would make birdie to card a third-round 69.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Filippo Celli took a share of the lead heading into the final round of the tournament, but got very lucky on the 18th hole

"I'm very happy because today was very tough," the 26-year-old Italian said. "It was windy out there. So I'm happy with how I handled the situation. Sometimes the wind changed a bit, so it wasn't easy.

"I was very patient through the front nine because I knew that on the back nine, I could have like more chances to make some birdies."

Elvira also made a birdie on his last hole, to post a four-under 68, and said after his round he "feels ready" to claim his debut tournament on the DP World Tour.

Plenty of other high-profile players also remain firmly in contention at the top of a bunched leaderboard, with Robert MacIntyre impressing to go five under through what was a flawless, bogey-free back nine, as he rose to tied-11th at 10 under par, alongside Ludvig Åberg, Ryan Fox, Matt Wallace and Sam Bairstow.

"That was a grind out there," Scott, who had to battle to move to finish two shots off the lead, said. "I saw all these good scores up on the board, but it didn't feel like that was really doable.

Image: Co-leader Manuel Elvira is out to win his debut tournament on the DP World Tour

"It was one step forward and a couple of steps back out there. Very hard to get in a rhythm. Hard to feel like you had a number where you could attack."

Elsewhere, first round co-leader Aaron Rai struggled to advance his score on Saturday, as he finished his day at nine under par. Matt Fitzpatrick, meanwhile, surged up the leaderboard to tie his compatriot, Rai, three back from the lead, alongside halfway leader Ryan Gerard, Alex Noren and Jordan Smith.

McIlroy: I will play aggressively if I need to

It felt like the Northern Irishman was looking for a spark throughout his third round, with McIlroy battling to go one over through his front nine.

The eighth hole has been his nemesis all week, with McIlroy cancelling out an early birdie on the fourth with a bogey on the eighth before adding another on the ninth.

It means McIlroy has gone three over on the eighth hole over his first three rounds.

The reigning Masters champion, who can usurp Patrick Reed at the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings with a second-place finish at the top of the leaderboard this week, found his groove, making birdie on the 12th, thanks to some excellent chipping.

He ended his third round with a flourish, striping a three-wood 375 yards down the fairway on the 17th hole on his way to make birdie, before stuffing an approach from 230 yards out to within a few feet of the hole.

McIlroy holed out for eagle to an enormous roar from the fans in the grandstand.

With so many players in contention, and crucial Race to Dubai rankings points in the balance for the world No 2, McIlroy insisted he would play aggressively on the back nine.

"There are a lot of people around the leaders. I think the conditions over the last couple of days are the reason why no one has got away from the pack, just because it has played so tricky and difficult.

Sports.title: Donnarumma: Man City are not in transition, it's going to be a great season
Sports.content:
"This is who we are. This is our team. This is City."

It's been a few days since the Manchester Derby victory but sat at Man City's training ground, Gianluigi Donnarumma is still basking in the glory.

He's not interested in Erling Haaland's controversial winner - though he's still annoyed Phil Foden was "harshly" sent off earlier in the game - as something else pleased him. A man down, everything going against them - City showed mettle and won.

"I loved my team-mates' performance, it was sublime," he tells Sky Sports. "The capacity to stay in the game and to react to difficult moments - no one can take that away from us.

"We will give everything for this shirt, for this club that gives us so much and offers us so much great support. It has a great history, and we need to give a lot back to it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Manchester United’s match against Manchester City in the Premier League

Not many had City down to hold a 100 per cent record this season ahead of the upcoming, lengthy international break - especially after losing the core of a successful era in Pep Guardiola, Bernardo Silva, John Stones and Rodri.

City have not been entirely convincing in certain areas - even Donnarumma says there is still lots to learn despite the faultless start to the Enzo Maresca era. But this was meant to be a transition season at City.

"I don't really like the word 'transition.'" he adds. "The club's objective is to win. This team's objective is to win. We'll certainly give everything we can to achieve that.

"We could reach the end of the season having won something, or having won nothing. But what's important is having a winning mentality, going out there and trying to win everything we possibly can."

Part of that winning mentality is being driven by Donnarumma - who is part of a newly-formed leadership group that replaced the likes of Bernardo, Stones and Rodri.

Donnarumma sits alongside Ruben Dias in the leadership pecking order, along with Haaland and Marc Guehi. All four players have one thing in common: they all have won trophies both at City and at other clubs in their careers.

Image: Man City have won four games from four at the start of this Premier League season

So as the likes of Ayyoub Bouaddi, Elliot Anderson and Iliman Ndiaye settle into their new team - tasked with making an immediate impact in a non-transition year - the leadership quartet are there to drive the standards.

"We've changed a few players. A few new ones have arrived," says Donnarumma. "They're all top players who are used to playing on the biggest stages, dealing with certain situations, and playing in the Premier League.

"It's not easy at the beginning when you move to a new club, a new organisation, a new city. But they're adapting well, and we're making them feel comfortable.

"The players who were already here are helping them a lot. I think we're going to have a great season.

"The objective is to get to the end and compete for everything there is to compete for - in addition to the Premier League, there's the Champions League and the two domestic cups."

It's a clear warning from City that anything is possible when it comes to this team. But when it comes to Donnarumma's aim of challenging for the Premier League and the Champions League, one team stands in the way: Arsenal.

Mikel Arteta's side also started the season with four straight league wins (before their defeat to Brighton) - and have the added recent psychological boost of pipping City to the Premier League post last May.

The recent Guardiola documentary showed down and disappointed scenes from City players as they slipped up at Bournemouth to hand the Gunners the title. Donnarumma - who had won the league title in each of the previous five seasons before last term - was one of them.

Image: Donnarumma missed out on the league title to Arsenal

"It's difficult, but that's football, that's life. You're not on your own," he says about that disappointment. "There are other strong teams, especially in the Premier League.

"It's not that if you don't win there isn't disappointment - of course there is - but it can happen because there are other teams as well, just like in the Champions League.

"It's important to go into every game trying to win it. Certainly, our objective will be to win, but there are other teams too.

"You have to compete, you have to work, and you have to do everything possible because the history of this club demands it."

Manchester City

Sunderland Sunday 20th September 1:00pm Kick off 2:00pm

Will it be City and Arsenal again competing at the top come May? "I don't know. We're only four games into the season," says the Italian goalkeeper.

But the stall has been set out. "Our focus right now has to be on working and trying to win every game. That has to be our objective.

"Whether we achieve it in the end or not, only time will tell."

Sports.title: Will Carrick navigate choppy waters to steer Man Utd ship back on course?
Sports.content:
Manchester United's Carabao Cup second-round loss at Grimsby last season was a result that many will remember.

It was a defeat which became synonymous with former Manchester United head coach Ruben Amorim's time in charge.

That was a very bad night for United, and although Wednesday's defeat at home to Brighton did not feel as significant, there were similarities for the man who succeeded Amorim, Michael Carrick.

Fulham

Manchester United Sunday 20th September 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

Man Utd's captain for the loss, Youri Tielemans, admitted afterwards that once they went 2-0 down, his side stopped playing - and that was pretty evident by their performance.

You could sense at Old Trafford from 20 minutes onwards that Brighton were in the ascendancy and the game was only going to go one way. Despite bringing on Bruno Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha, United failed to make an impression.

That is what will truly worry head coach Carrick.

After the few defeats Carrick has suffered since his return to the club in January, he has always backed his players or found positive qualities in the performances, but there was no such redemption to be found against Brighton.

Predictable problems and defensive worries

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Carabao Cup match between Manchester United and Brighton

When Carrick and his staff first came in, they deservedly received a lot of praise.

Defensively they looked tight and compact and that led to impressive wins against Manchester City and Arsenal.

The likes of Steve Holland, Jonathan Woodgate and Jonny Evans made an immediate improvement to the defensive unit.

But, equally, questions have to be raised now about the frailties that same defence is showing this season. Carrick's side have conceded two goals in three of their four Premier League games.

The defence was exposed once again in the Brighton loss. Yes, one goal was a goalkeeping error by Karl Darlow, but aside from the goals conceded, the shape and understanding of the back four lacked any sort of coherence.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Dave Reed analyses Man Utd's running stats

Left-back predictably is an issue for Carrick. He has yet to acknowledge the area as a specific weakness as per his style when engaging in the media, but it is a significant problem - one the United hierarchy knew about going into the summer's transfer window.

Luke Shaw, United's only senior left-back at the club, has missed the last three games through a minor injury, but considering his age and injury track record - despite his excellent availability last season - it was naive not to strengthen in that area.

Carrick has experimented with Noussair Mazraoui in that position but he seems to have fallen down the pecking order, as the less experienced Patrick Dorgu was preferred for the Manchester derby loss.

Young left-back Harry Amass does not seem to be fancied in the position long-term either - so how will United remedy the position for the rest of the season?

An awkward discussion over Carrick's future

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carrick responds to the Old Trafford boos after Manchester United were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton

It seems ridiculous to even discuss Carrick's job security after only a few weeks of the new season.

Man Utd have still accumulated the most points across the league since his return in January.

However, as Carrick admitted himself, a few moments such as Ainsley Maitland-Niles' equaliser for Everton, City's controversial VAR goal and now a shocking collapse against Brighton, have made it all feel very different.

If United lose at Fulham on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, there will be inevitable and uncomfortable discussions around whether Carrick can lead United out of the storm they currently find themselves in.

That may be for another day, but the United head coach does deserve sympathy for the squad he has been dealt.

The lack of sales and outgoings this summer at United handicapped them in being able to further reinforce the squad. But does that excuse them ignoring key areas to strengthen?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp rips into Manchester United for the way they defended in their 3-2 loss to Brighton in the Carabao Cup third round

The left-back area, as mentioned, should have been strengthened. Knowing Benjamin Sesko was still nursing a shin injury all summer, perhaps United should have brought in a temporary No 9 to share the load rather than playing Mbeumo and Cunha out of position. Both players have failed to discover the form they showed under Carrick last season.

But, ultimately, until United are able to be in a position where they can really reshape their team in one window, they will continue to be caught in this cycle of strengthening just enough with players left over from previous regimes.

That perhaps is why you could hear boos at Old Trafford after the Brighton loss. Not just aimed at that performance, but perhaps a familiar feeling of a cycle beginning again, a deja vu of seasons past and another false dawn after a promising start under a new United head coach.

Again, it feels too soon for that just yet, and Carrick deserves time after what he delivered last season, but these are the waters he has to navigate, and ultimately, he will be the one judged.

But if he can stop the spiral, even without a win against Fulham with a positive performance, time may allow him to be able to steer the ship back on course.

Sports.title: Littler scrapes past Aspinall in World Series of Darts Finals
Sports.content:
Luke Littler moved a step closer to his first clean sweep of majors in one year with a hard-fought win over Nathan Aspinall in Amsterdam.

Littler, the 2024 champion who was beaten 11-7 by Michael van Gerwen in last year's final, edged out Aspinall 10-9 in the World Series of Darts Finals second round, taking the last two legs in a see-saw contest and sealing victory with a 12-dart break.

Following the win in the Dutch capital, Littler said: "Nathan pushed me all the way tonight; I didn't feel confident in the first two sessions, but I managed to make it 6-6 and I was very good in the final session.

Image: Littler celebrates during his victory over Aspinall (credit: Kelly Deckers/PDC)

"When I came here two years ago, Ross Smith missed darts to beat me and then I went on to win the title, but I know it will be a good test against Jonny (Clayton) tomorrow (Sunday).

"I'm glad that the streak is still on, but it's going to be very tough."

Earlier on Saturday, Gerwyn Price defeated Jim Long 10-5 and James Wade saw off Wessel Nijman 10-7.

Luke Humphries crashed out with 10-9 defeat to Dirk van Duijvenbode, in the afternoon session, while Josh Rock secured a 10-7 win over Ryan Searle and Ross Smith beat Daryl Gurney 10-5.

An emotional Van Duijvenbode, who was joined by young son Levi on stage after the match, said: "Having my kid here is the best thing in my life.

"I won this game because he was here. When you are playing against the world number two you are always nervous.

Image: Dirk van Duijvenbode celebrates his victory over Luke Humphries (credit: Kelly Deckers/PDC)

"When I looked up at him he made so happy every time. It made me so relaxed. In the end that is the reason I won it."

Gian van Veen prevailed 10-7 against Karel Sedlacek and now faces Van Duijvenbode in an all-Dutch quarter-final, while Jonny Clayton battled past Motomu Sakai 10-8 to set up his showdown with Littler.

The semi-finals and final will take place from 6pm on Sunday, following the quarter-finals in the afternoon.

Sports.title: Curtain falls on historic Peters era at Hull KR
Sports.content:
In 2025 Hull KR became just the fifth team to win the Super League Grand Final in the 30 years of the competition.

That was thanks to the guidance of Willie Peters. In his third year in charge of the club, he helped them 'climb Everest' and make history.

Not only did they win the Betfred Super League, they picked up the League Leaders' Shield and Challenge Cup, and then topped that off with a World Club Challenge win over Brisbane Broncos.

Every trophy was theirs. They simply were the team to beat, but no one could.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League eliminator between Warrington Wolves and Hull KR as Matty Ashton's hat-trick helped the hosts book a semi-final against Leeds Rhinos

It was announced part way through this season that 2026 would mark Peters' final season in charge of the Robins before he heads to pastures new to take charge of the NRL's newest franchise, the PNG Chiefs.

The task was set: Finish on a high for their leader. Unfortunately for those from east Hull, they did not get the fairytale ending to close out Peters' four years in charge as they went out in the eliminators to Warrington Wolves after finishing sixth in the table.

However, Peters views it as "the best four years of his life" of which he is immensely proud.

"Discipline has cost us a lot this year, and unfortunately tonight, but I can't fault them," Peters told Sky Sports after the defeat at Warrington.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Peta Hiku is shown a straight red card for throwing a rabbit punch, leaving Hull KR down to 12-men in their Super League eliminator against Warrington Wolves

"I am really proud of them. They kept fighting to the end. Warrington played really well and have been a very good team all year. I wish them all the best, but I'm really, really proud of the group and proud of what they've achieved over the last four years at the club. We've made a lot of beautiful memories.

"When you're down to 12 men it makes it difficult, but we put ourselves in the game. We scored down the other end, went two points ahead and then, against the run of play, they scored.

"Fatigue always creeps in and it did towards the back end of the game. Peta (Hiku) has been great for us for three years. What he did [get sent off] was probably the wrong thing, but he's been outstanding for me over the last three years.

"We've got a lot of great memories, that's for sure, but they're still here, still cheering for their team. We're a close-knit club. We're a club that wanted to win trophies, and we have, but the fight tonight shows what this place is about.

"We were well beaten, but we still showed a lot of fight. My family and I have had an absolute ball. We've loved it over here and we'll never forget our time at Hull KR.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joe Burgess finishes a superb length-of-the-field Hull KR move after Arthur Mourgue slices through the Warrington defence

"I do feel loved, absolutely. Love's important. I remember Russell Crowe saying years ago at South (Sydney Rabbitohs) that it's all about the love, and there's something in that.

"When you're part of a family and create the right environment, especially in sport, where everyone cares about each other, you can do wonderful things.

"There's no doubt I've felt the love from the fans and the players, and vice versa. I love them too. When there's genuine care and love for each other, you can achieve special things.

"I love it over here. I'm really looking forward to the next chapter and to having a positive impact on a country (Papua New Guinea) through rugby league, both on and off the field.

"It's similar to what we've done here, but on a bigger scale. I'm really excited about that challenge."

Peters to return to Super League one day? 'Never say never'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League Grand Final between Hull KR and Wigan Warriors

While this particular chapter is closed for Peters and he has ticked off his goal of coaching in Super League, he admits he will never close the book on the UK.

But for now, he is focused on achieving the next goal which is being a head coach in the NRL.

Despite that, he will continue to back the European competition and ensure it gets the "recognition it deserves".

"We have loved it here. This has been home, and probably this year was the first time it really felt like home, which made it even harder knowing I was leaving. My family and I have loved it, so you never say never," he added.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Hull KR celebrate their historic domestic treble with a bus parade around the city

"I am proud. I've got a great support network and I've loved working with everyone. You've all been great. The rugby league community over here has been fantastic. The game is in a positive place and I think there's a lot of growth ahead in the next few years.

"The product is outstanding and it's finally getting the recognition it deserves, even in Australia.

"I don't think Super League has always received the respect it merits, but I've always respected it. That's why I played here and why I always wanted to coach here.

"I'm proud to have been involved in Super League as a coach, and now I've got some goals to tick off when I return to the NRL.

"Just thank you for the memories and thank you for the support they've given me. They've made me a better person and a better coach.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the World Club Challenge between Hull KR and Brisbane Broncos

"I've now got an opportunity to return to the NRL, something I've always wanted to do, and it's purely because of what they've achieved.

"At the end of the day, the players decide how hard they want to work and where they want to get to, and they've been massive for me and my family.

"I also want to acknowledge the board, who have been incredibly supportive. Everyone at Hull KR, I'm going to miss dearly. Thank you to everyone, including the away fans. The support I've received has been incredible. So, thank you."

Sports.title: Brighton demolish champions Arsenal 3-0 to mark anniversary in style
Sports.content:
So much for the new Invincibles. Arsenal were brought back down to earth with a shuddering bump by a scintillating display from Brighton as Fabian Hürzeler’s vibrant side celebrated the club’s 125th anniversary in style.

The special edition shirts they wore to mark the occasion will end up being collector’s items after the Premier League champions were ripped apart. Arsenal were attempting to record an eighth successive victory in all competitions to start the new campaign for the first time since 1903 when they were still known as Woolwich Arsenal.

Instead, it is Brighton – inspired by first-half goals from the veteran stand-in captain, Pascal Gross, and the exciting teenager Charalampos Kostoulas – who find themselves in third place, two points behind Arsenal. New signing Chema Andrés made the points safe from a corner 12 minutes into the second half. That meant Arsenal conceded three goals for the first time since December 2023 in all competitions and Mikel Arteta will be most concerned that it could easily have been more against the division’s top scorers, 16 in five games.

The home supporters waved blue and white flags before kick-off as the players swapped their usual kits for a deep blue limited edition shirt that was inspired by their first season in Southern League Division Two in 1901. That has caused controversy among fans after originally being listed on sale for £150 in a package that included a letter of authenticity from the club owner, Tony Bloom, and a keyring. Given this is the only time they will wear it, those who shelled out will be pleased they did now.

What has made Brighton’s goalscoring exploits so impressive is that they have managed it almost completely without their first-choice attack due to injury, while last year’s top scorer, Danny Welbeck, was sold to Chelsea in the summer. Georginio Rutter returned as a late substitute, but the damage had already been inflicted by then thanks to Gross and Kostoulas.

Jurriën Timber looked leggy on his first start since March and Bruno Guimarães was disappointing on his first Premier League start for Arsenal. Myles Lewis-Skelly’s energy and drive in midfield was sorely missed in the week he was recalled to the England squad.

View image in fullscreen Pascal Gross fires home Brighton’s first goal against Arsenal. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

From the first whistle, Kostoulas – signed last summer for £30m – led Brighton’s fearsome press that provoked Arsenal into a number of uncharacteristic errors, including a misplaced pass from Guimarães that forced David Raya to tip a deflected effort from the 19-year-old around the post. Raya was also guilty of donating possession to the lively Yasin Ayari in a dangerous position. Arsenal and Arteta looked rattled for the first time this season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Christos Tzolis could not take a rare opportunity on the break after being picked out by Bukayo Saka and they were made to pay for it just after the half-hour mark. Perhaps wary of the unmarked Ayari to their left, Gabriel Magalhães and Riccardo Calafiori were slow to challenge Gross when he received the ball on the edge of Arsenal’s area from Kostoulas and the veteran picked his spot perfectly off the inside of the post.

Ayari came close to doubling the lead five minutes before half-time when he fired into the side-netting before Kostoulas did. Saka had just spurned a great chance to equalise after being set up by Martin Ødegaard and once again Gabriel was guilty of ball watching as the Greek striker thumped the ball past Raya from 25 yards.

Arteta immediately sent out Max Dowman, who scored two goals against Ipswich in midweek, to warm up. He must have been tempted to throw the 16-year-old on at the start of the second half as Kostoulas went close again for Brighton.

It was too late once Andrés nodded in at the far post from a pinpoint Gross corner. “Are you Tottenham in disguise?” sang the delighted Brighton fans.

Arteta introduced Dowman with 10 minutes remaining as he emptied his bench. But having been knocked off the top of the Premier League on goal difference courtesy of this heavy loss, there will be plenty of soul-searching during the three-week international break for the Arsenal manager.

Sports.title: De Zerbi rips into Spurs players after Villa defeat: ‘Disappointed, sad and frustrated’
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi tore into his failing Tottenham team after their 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa, saying “we can’t lose the game in this way”. The Italian headed straight down the tunnel at full time, but was once again forced to endure boos as Tottenham went into the three-week international break without a Premier League victory to their name and just two points on the board.

De Zerbi criticised his team’s mentality, but also the physical condition of his players, and said the substitute Mohammed Kudus had disrupted the balance of his team.

“I am very disappointed, sad and frustrated for the performance,” De Zerbi said. “We can’t lose the game in this way, we can’t concede the second goal, we can’t lose balance just because we are losing. I spoke with our four attackers in minute 51, I asked them to use their head, all second half I was telling people to be calm. But the second goal was incredible.”

Jackson scored in the 67th minute after latching on to a long kick by the impressive Zion Suzuki. De Zerbi said his players had been prepped to deal with the Villa goalkeeper’s clearances, but had switched off.

“We knew this season Aston Villa are playing 86% more long balls than last season and we spoke in many meetings about it,” De Zerbi said. “Now we have to explain another game like [the home defeat against] Newcastle where we played the first half well, got to 60 minutes OK, and then we lose.”

Quick Guide How do I 

With players now heading out to play for their national sides, De Zerbi said he had left them with no parting message. “I didn’t speak with the players because I didn’t want to say anything. The players who go with the national team have to play and work. For sure we have to work more because I didn’t like the finish to this game. We can’t say everything is bad, but it is not enough.”

For Unai Emery, a first Premier League victory of the season a reminder to his players of the style of play that has resulted in success for Villa in recent seasons. “The players did well because they believed,” he said.
